_disclaimer: Published-literature summary, not a formulary or prescription. Every entry must be presented with its evidence_tier and source. No entry here is an FDA-approved dose. Always recommend confirmation with a licensed veterinarian.

evidence_tiers.A: Randomized controlled trial in the target species/condition
evidence_tiers.B: Non-randomized clinical study, case series, or single RCT not yet replicated
evidence_tiers.C: Safety/tolerance study in healthy animals (not disease-specific efficacy)
evidence_tiers.D: Consumer/practical guidance not sourced to a peer-reviewed study

conditions.dose_range: 2 mg/kg CBD, twice daily (studied range 2-8 mg/kg/day)
conditions.notes: Studied as adjunct to conventional multimodal analgesia, not monotherapy replacement.
conditions.source: Gamble et al. 2018, Frontiers in Veterinary Science

conditions.dose_range: Not uniformly reported as a single figure across trials; used as add-on to standard anti-epileptic drugs
conditions.notes: CBD studied strictly as adjunct to existing AEDs, reduced seizure frequency vs. placebo in add-on arm.
conditions.source: McGrath et al. 2019 JAVMA; Rozental et al. 2023 J Vet Intern Med (51 dogs, crossover)

conditions.dose_range: Not independently published in detail here; single trial only
conditions.notes: ~65% of treated dogs showed >=50% reduction in itch/chew behavior; about half fully resolved. Single trial, not yet replicated.
conditions.source: CannPal canine atopic dermatitis study, summarized by Cornell Riney Canine Health Center

conditions.dose_range: ~4 mg/kg/day well tolerated over 6 months; escalating-dose studies tolerated up to 10-20 mg/kg/day short-term
conditions.notes: Recurring mild ALP elevation reported across studies; monitor liver enzymes on long courses.
conditions.source: Bradley/Bakke et al. 2022 Frontiers in Vet Science; Deabold et al. 2019 Animals

conditions.dose_range: 0.1-0.5 mg/kg, split BID, reassess at 5-7 days before increasing
conditions.notes: Not RCT-sourced; typical of commercial pet-CBD product guidance.

conditions.dose_range: 4 mg/kg/day THC-free CBD distillate, well tolerated over 26 weeks
conditions.notes: Longest published feline CBD safety study. Persistent ALT elevation noted in at least one cat; monitor ALT at baseline and ~6 weeks.
conditions.source: Coltherd et al. 2023/2024, Frontiers in Veterinary Science

conditions.condition: acute tolerance ceiling (not a therapeutic dose)
conditions.dose_range: single doses up to 80 mg/kg tolerated short-term
conditions.notes: Safety-study ceiling only; do not present as a treatment recommendation.

conditions.condition: any specific feline disease (osteoarthritis, CKD-related inflammation, etc.)
conditions.dose_range: no disease-specific efficacy RCT yet published in cats
conditions.notes: Major evidence gap - flag explicitly rather than extrapolate from dog data or healthy-cat safety data.

conditions.dose_range: 0.1-0.5 mg/kg, start low, cats are more sensitive than dogs
conditions.notes: Conflicts with some consumer sources claiming cats need 2x the per-lb dog dose; peer-reviewed safety data supports starting low, not high.

conditions.dose_range: 0.5-3 mg/kg studied across pharmacokinetic and small clinical trials
conditions.notes: No confirmed synovial fluid penetration of CBD despite joint-relief marketing; CBDA reaches much higher serum levels than CBD at equivalent oral dose.
conditions.source: Interlandi et al. 2024; Yocom/Contino et al.; 2025 AJVR chronic dosing safety study

conditions.notes: FEI reclassified CBD/CBDA from prohibited to controlled medication in 2022; detection can still trigger an adverse analytical finding. Always check competition status before recommending.
conditions.source: Frontiers in Vet Science, Connemara pony PK study, 2026

conditions.condition: any condition, any food-producing species (cattle, swine, poultry, sheep, goats, etc.)
conditions.dose_range: NONE - no FDA/AAFCO-approved cannabinoid ingredient exists for food-producing animals
conditions.notes: Do not provide a dose. State clearly that no ingredient is approved, cite human food-residue concern, refer to state department of agriculture / feed control office.
conditions.source: AAFCO position statements; FDA-CVM feed ingredient approval status; CDFA HempCBD Notice
